analysis.title: Round Trip: Tech Hedge Funds Wipe Out Their Entire 2026 Gain As Nasdaq Suffers Worst Day Since Covid
key_insights: Goldman Prime Services estimates TMT hedge funds fell more than 4% on Thursday and are now roughly flat to slightly positive YTD. They were up about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off.

Goldman prime book moves at the US close: Global Fundamental L/S -1.3% (-2 SD, mainly market/beta), US-focused funds -1.7% (-2.9 SD), European funds -48bps, multi-strats -1.4% (-2.3 SD, assuming 4.5x leverage and no fees), Systematic L/S +0.2%. YTD: Fundamental L/S +8.7%, US-focused +5.5%, systematic +16%.

NDX fell about 6.35% to 26,630, about 15% below its highs, and semis fell about 12%+, nearly 40% off their highs. Both had their biggest 1-day drawdowns since March 2020. Goldman's desk says rallies were sold all day and the close was on the lows.
The Nasdaq 100 had its worst day since March 9, 2020. The S&P 500 fell 4.36%, its worst since April 4, 2025. VVIX jumped nearly 45 points, the 2nd largest 1-day move on record behind Volmageddon.
High Beta Momentum fell 6.2% and is 51% off its June highs, its worst drawdown in over a decade. Goldman says many of its AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.

Goldman's Callahan frames the market's question as what is priced in for datacenter capex and gigawatt builds, more in 2028+ than in 2027. SOX multiples have compressed by about 50% from the June/July highs. Bottom-up data (memory pricing, compute pricing, 3Q earnings) is still strong while the top-down (policy, datacenter construction debates) has gotten harder.

Goldman sees local data center moratoria freezing up to 45% of planned capacity. Selling was most evident in engineering and construction stocks, IPP/power, neoclouds and semiconductors. Goldman credit strategist Lynam expects the moratoria to be short-lived but sees near-term credit risks tilted toward spread widening.
Hyperscalers have issued $296 billion of debt this year against Goldman's full-year forecast of $250 billion. The article also cites ING reportedly shopping a $500 million data center loan book.

Goldman's floor reported inbound calls at 10/10 but activity at about 5 on a 1-10 scale. Price action was driven by macro instruments, with large notionals in ETFs. Asset managers were net sellers of semis and AI, there was no offsetting bid for hyperscalers or defensive tech as on Wednesday, and hedge fund flows were roughly balanced while toggling short books aggressively.
ETFs were about 32% of volume, the largest share since June, on roughly 27 billion shares. Options volume was the highest in market history, including a record number of puts.

Systematic supply is large. Futures closed below Goldman's medium-term CTA threshold at 7,549, and the 2.5-stdev down scenario already had $7.48 billion of S&P for sale over the next week. Nomura's McElligott estimated $47 billion of levered ETF selling and $61 billion of vol control supply.

Nomura's McElligott says clients feel further incentivized to take risk down after hedge fund performance headlines, aiming to preserve what remains of YTD performance into next year. UBS's desk reported hedge fund flows at 23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell.

Vanda Research flagged massive retail selling of US single stocks in the first 30 minutes, the largest 30-minute episode since October. After the late-July capitulation, retail selling lasted several days. Vanda says to look for institutional buying to help any recovery.

Vanda expects CTAs to turn outright short the Nasdaq 100 after the break of 27,600, and says a clean break below 26,800 would take CTA exposure to Liberation Day lows. The NDX closed at 26,630. Callahan notes the NDX is re-testing a multi-year base trendline that held in April 2025 and March 2026.
Semis underperformed the S&P by more than 15 points over five days, the biggest underperformance since 2002.

Asia followed. Wire headlines had TSMC down 9.8% and the Taiex down 9%. South Korea halted trading with a marketwide circuit breaker after the Kospi fell more than 8% at the open and eased margin rules for three months.
After the bell, NET rose 15%, LRCX announced a buyback of about $25 billion, ABNB rose 10% and FROG rose 22%.
October payrolls are due Friday morning. Goldman economists expect +75K versus a +65K consensus and a three-month average of +51K, with average hourly earnings up 0.3% m/m.

The author's view is that flows say the selloff is not finished: TMT funds are flat on the year, retail selling persisted after the July capitulation, CTAs are flipping short, and the desk saw few shopping-list conversations. The author expects hedge funds to keep selling into any payrolls bounce.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose 15% after the bell on a re-acceleration to +39% y/y growth, its best in about 4 years, per Goldman's Callahan.
Announced a buyback of about $25 billion, roughly 10% of its market cap.

Shares rose 10% after the bell on room-night growth re-accelerating to +16% y/y. About 40% of support issues were resolved without a human agent in Q3 and support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y.
Shares rose 22% after the bell as cloud revenue accelerated to +60% y/y.
Wire headlines had TSMC down 9.8% in Asia trading after the US selloff, with the Taiex down 9%.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is down about 12%+ on the day and nearly 40% off its highs, with multiples compressed about 50% from the June/July highs. Goldman's desk questions whether slowdowns are already over-priced and says supply from asset managers continues.

sector_views.sector: Data center construction, power and neoclouds
sector_views.rationale: Selling was most evident in E&C, IPP/power and neoclouds after the local data center moratoria news, which Goldman says could freeze up to 45% of planned capacity.

earnings_insights: 3Q earnings season has delivered strong bottom-up data (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings), yet stocks keep falling, per Goldman's Callahan.
NET reported after the bell on Thursday: growth re-accelerated to +39% y/y, its best in about 4 years (basis not specified in the article). Shares +15%.

ABNB reported after the bell on Thursday: room-night growth re-accelerated to +16% y/y. About 40% of Q3 customer support issues were resolved without a human agent and support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y. Shares +10%.
FROG reported after the bell on Thursday: cloud revenue accelerated to +60% y/y. Shares +22%.
LRCX announced a buyback of about $25 billion, roughly 10% of its market cap.
Callahan's list of AI and AI-adjacent names now flat or down on the year includes CRDO, AMKR, AVGO, QCOM, NVDA, SNPS, CDNS, COHR, PLTR, MDB and others.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman economists cite the low level of layoffs and big data indicators of job growth. The forecast is above consensus, so a print near it would not add to the growth-scare read.
The consensus compares with a three-month average of +51K. The report is released Friday morning, and the author expects hedge funds to sell into any bounce it produces.
Context for the October forecasts. Both estimates sit above the recent trend.

macro_indicators.indicator: October average hourly earnings m/m (Goldman forecast)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman's expectation alongside its payrolls call.

risk_factors: Further hedge fund de-grossing as funds protect residual YTD performance into year-end.
Systematic supply from CTAs, vol control and levered ETFs if the NDX loses 26,800.
Retail selling that persists for days, as after the late-July capitulation, with no institutional bid.
Data center moratoria and uncertainty over 2028+ capex and gigawatt builds.
AI-related debt issuance (hyperscalers at $296 billion YTD against Goldman's $250 billion forecast) and credit spread widening, with the junk end of the AI debt market already cracking.
Payrolls on Friday morning as a near-term event risk.
charts_described: Callahan flags the NDX re-testing the base trendline that held for the past few years, closing at 26,630, a hair above the line that caught it in April 2025 and March 2026.
Semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 15 points over the past five days, the biggest bout of underperformance since 2002.
vol_and_positioning: VVIX jumped nearly 45 points, the 2nd largest 1-day move ever behind Volmageddon. McElligott's intraday VVIX reading was 122 and kept rising into the close.
Record options volume including a record number of puts. ETFs were about 32% of the tape, the largest share since June.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold at 7,549, implying incremental US supply. The 2.5-stdev down scenario had $7.48 billion of S&P for sale over the next week.
Nomura estimated $47 billion of levered ETF selling and $61 billion of vol control supply, and warned the usual 2-3pm low-then-rally might not occur. Goldman says the market closed on the lows.
Vanda sees CTAs turning outright short the Nasdaq 100 after 27,600 broke. A clean break below 26,800 would take CTA exposure to Liberation Day lows. The NDX closed at 26,630.
Goldman's hedge fund VIP basket had its worst day since 2011 about two weeks ago, with nets pushed to a one-year low.
Hedge fund flows at UBS ran 23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell. Goldman's desk saw hedge funds toggling short books aggressively.
Vanda flagged the largest 30-minute retail selling episode in US single stocks since October. Names held by Situational Awareness in June were among the heavy retail sales.
RSIs on NDX and semis are oversold, the first time for the NDX since Liberation Day, per Callahan.
geopolitical: South Korea halted trading with a marketwide circuit breaker after the Kospi fell more than 8% at the open and eased margin rules for three months.
Local moratoria on data center construction (the 'Blue Tsunami' on Tuesday) could freeze up to 45% of planned capacity, per Goldman.
Post-election hedge monetization on Wednesday preceded the selloff.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Prime Services desk estimates TMT funds down more than 4%, while Goldman earlier told clients to buy the dip, per the article.
Citadel's Scott Rubner argued that semis at 13.8x look cheap on Thursday morning, before the Nasdaq dropped 6%.
UBS's trading desk reported hedge fund flows at 23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell, similar to Goldman's read of de-risking.
Nomura's McElligott and Vanda Research both flag CTA and systematic selling, consistent with Goldman's CTA threshold at 7,549.

tension_points.bull_case: SOX multiples have compressed about 50% from the June/July highs and Citadel's Rubner argued semis at 13.8x were cheap. Bottom-up data (memory pricing, compute pricing, 3Q earnings) remains strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Flows say the selloff is not done. TMT funds are flat YTD with eight weeks left, CTAs are turning short, retail selling persisted for days after July, and Goldman's desk saw almost no shopping-list conversations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Institutional buying that leads a recovery, which Vanda says to look for. Conversely, a clean NDX break below 26,800 would deepen CTA selling.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman credit strategist Lynam says the data center moratoria should be short-lived.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers have issued $296 billion of debt YTD against a $250 billion forecast, and Goldman sees near-term risks firmly tilted toward spread widening. The junk end of the AI debt market is already cracking.
